# Esther Chapter 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 458r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EST_007_page_001.jpg

---

**7:1** And-the-king and-Haman came to-drink [lishtot] with-Ester the-queen [ha-malkah]. **7:2** And-the-king said to-Ester also on-the-day the-second [ha-sheni] at-the-banquet [mishteh] of-the-wine [ha-yayin], "What [is] your-petition [she'elatekh], Ester the-queen? And-it-shall-be-given [ve-tinnaten] to-you. And-what [is] your-request [baqqashatekh]? Up-to half [chatsi] the-kingdom [ha-malkhut], and-it-shall-be-done [ve-te'as]."

**7:3** And-Ester the-queen answered [va-ta'an] and-said, "If I-have-found favor [chen] in-your-eyes [be-einekha], O-king, and-if upon the-king [it-is] good [tov], let-my-life [nafshi] be-given [tinnaten] to-me at-my-petition [bi-she'elati], and-my-people [ammi] at-my-request [be-vaqqashati]. **7:4** For we-have-been-sold [nimkarnu], I and-my-people, to-be-destroyed [le-hashmid], to-be-slain [la-harog], and-to-be-annihilated [u-le'abbed]. And-if as-slaves [la-avadim] and-as-maidservants [ve-lishfachot] we-had-been-sold [nimkarnu], I-would-have-kept-silent [hecherashti], for [ki] the-distress [ha-tsar] is-not equal [einennu shoveh] to-the-damage [be-nezeq] of-the-king."

**7:5** And-the-king Achashverosh said, and-he-said to-Ester the-queen, "Who [is] he [hu-zeh], and-where [is] he [ve-ei-zeh hu], whose-heart [libbo] has-filled-him [mela'o] to-do thus [la'asot ken]?" **7:6** And-Ester said, "A-man [ish], an-adversary [tsar] and-an-enemy [ve-oyev] — this wicked [ha-ra ha-zeh] Haman!" And-Haman was-terrified [niv'at] before [mi-lifney] the-king and-the-queen.

**7:7** And-the-king arose in-his-wrath [ba-chamato] from-the-banquet of-the-wine [mishteh ha-yayin] [and went] to-the-garden [ginnat] of-the-palace [ha-bitan], and-Haman stood [amad] to-plead [le-vaqqesh] for his-life [nafsho] from [me'im] Ester the-queen, for he-saw [ra'ah] that evil [ha-ra'ah] was-determined [kaltah] against-him from-with [me'et] the-king.

**7:8** And-the-king returned [shav] from-the-garden of-the-palace to the-house [beyt] of-the-banquet of-the-wine, and-Haman was-falling [nofel] upon the-couch [ha-mittah] on-which Ester [was]. And-the-king said, "Will-he-even [ha-gam] assault [likhbosh] the-queen with-me [immi] in-the-house [ba-bayit]?" The-word [ha-davar] went-out [yatsa] from-the-mouth [pi] of-the-king, and-the-face [penei] of-Haman they-covered [chafu].

**7:9** And-Charvonah, one of-the-eunuchs [ha-sarisim] before [lifney] the-king, said, "Also behold [hineh] the-gallows [ha-ets] which Haman made [asah] for-Mordekhai, who spoke [dibber] good [tov] for [al] the-king, is-standing [omed] in-the-house of-Haman — fifty cubits [chamishim ammah] high [gavoah]." And-the-king said, "Hang-him [teluhu] on-it." **7:10** And-they-hanged [va-yitlu] Haman on the-gallows [ha-ets] which he-had-prepared [hekhin] for-Mordekhai, and-the-wrath [chamat] of-the-king subsided [shakhakhah].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.4 — "the distress is not equal to the damage of the king":** The clause *ki ein ha-tsar shoveh be-nezeq ha-melekh* is notoriously difficult. The word *tsar* can mean "distress" or "adversary" (a wordplay with v.6 where Haman is called *tsar*). The phrase may mean: (a) "the adversary is not worthy of the king's damage/loss" (i.e., killing the Jews would harm the king's own interests), or (b) "the distress would not justify troubling the king." EMET renders the surface grammar while noting the ambiguity.

**v.5 — Double introduction "the king said, and he said":** The Masoretic text reads *va-yomer... va-yomer* — a doubled speech introduction rare in Hebrew narrative. Some suggest textual duplication; others read it as emphasis or agitation. EMET preserves the redundancy as it stands in the Leningrad Codex.

**v.8 — "nofel" (was falling):** The participle *nofel* indicates Haman was in the act of falling upon the couch — prostrating himself in desperation — when the king returned. The king's interpretation ("Will he even assault the queen?") is either genuine misreading or deliberate rhetorical escalation.

*— EMET*
